reading.body:
NTT Ashburn VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, ranking 14th of 26 Virginia data centers that disclose megawatts, while most of Virginia's 332 mapped facilities publish no capacity figure.

The 36 MW is 2.2 percent of Virginia's published 1,639.4 MW, a total that undercounts the state because only 26 of 332 mapped sites disclose capacity. Ashburn is Virginia's primary data center hub, and this facility sits there, but its grid connection and whether it is reserved for AI workloads are not published. At a common AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 36 MW corresponds to roughly 900 racks, or 1,100 to 1,400 accelerators depending on configuration.

The facility publishes no certifications and no announced expansion, and its suitability score of 68 rests on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. No grid connection details or workload reservation are published, so the data cannot confirm whether this facility supports AI training or inference. The disclosed capacity is real but partial, and the surrounding market remains largely unmeasured.
